newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tycoon says will sue in Russia privatisation row.
newsitem.headline: Tycoon says will sue in Russia privatisation row.

text.p: Vladimir Gusinsky, one of the Russian media and banking magnates involved in a political uproar over last week's controversial privatisation, said on Thursday he would sue the successful bidder for defamation.

In a statement read out at a news conference, Gusinsky denied allegations that he had tried to influence the sale of a quarter of the Svyazinvest state telecommunications company against the public interest.

Gusinsky's statement described as "lies" remarks by Uneximbank chief Vladimir Potanin, who led the winning consortium. Potanin was quoted by Interfax news agency as saying Gusinsky had tried to strike a "backroom deal" for the Svyazinvest stake.
He said his Most group, which includes Most-Bank and the influential Most-Media television and press concern, had not taken part in the bidding nor in any other privatisation auction.
The statement was read out by Gusinsky's spokesman Vyacheslav Kostikov, who warned that the political uproar, partly fueled by the tycoon's own media stable, could damage the government.

Kostikov was asked to confirm anonymous statements by top government officials that Gusinsky had flown to France last week for talks with First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais before the Svyazinvest auction. He said he had no information on the matter.
Kostikov said he was concerned that the "scandal" over the Svyazinvest sale could shake up the government, which has begun a new course of market reforms under Chubais and other young liberals.
Kostikov said he welcomed a decision by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to look into the sale.
